citeAs: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu (2017). Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art. Proceedings of the IEEE.
creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu (Northwestern Polytechnical University)
description: NWPU-RESISC45 is a large-scale, freely and publicly available benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification, created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU). It contains 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images per class, with image sizes of 256×256 pixels in RGB color space. The dataset covers more than 100 countries and regions worldwide, with spatial resolution varying from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel, and features rich variations in translation, viewpoint, object pose, spatial resolution, illumination, background, and occlusion.
name: NWPU-RESISC45
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Scene classes were first selected by investigating all scene classes of existing datasets to form 30 widely-used scene categories, then 15 additional meaningful scene classes were selected by searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales by experts in remote sensing image interpretation.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset was designed to address limitations of existing datasets including small scale of scene classes, small image numbers, lack of image variations and diversity, and saturation of accuracy. Fine-grained scene classes with high semantic overlapping (e.g., circular farmland and rectangular farmland, commercial area and industrial area, basketball court and tennis court) were deliberately included to increase within-class diversity and between-class similarity.
rai:dataCollection: Images were extracted by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth (Google Inc.), which maps the Earth by the superimposition of images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography and geographic information system (GIS) onto a 3D globe. The 31,500 images cover more than 100 countries and regions all over the world, including developing, transition, and highly developed economies.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) data accessed via Google Earth (Google Inc.). Images are in the red green blue (RGB) color space with spatial resolution varying from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel for most scene classes.
rai:dataLimitations: The classes of island, lake, mountain, and snowberg have lower spatial resolutions than the stated range of ~30 m to 0.2 m per pixel. Almost all scene classification methods rely on only traditional remote sensing (overhead imagery) to distinguish different types of land-cover, without incorporating social media or spatial technology data.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted and cropped to 256×256 pixels in RGB color space. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales to ensure rich variations in translation, viewpoint, object pose and appearance, spatial resolution, illumination, background, and occlusion.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables the development of intelligent earth observation systems for land use and land cover classification, natural hazards detection, environment monitoring, and urban planning. It supports the development of deep learning methods for remote sensing that can benefit a wide range of societal applications.
rai:dataUseCases: Remote sensing image scene classification, land use and land cover (LULC) determination, natural hazards detection, geospatial object detection, geographic image retrieval, vegetation mapping, environment monitoring, and urban planning. The dataset is intended to enable the community to develop and evaluate various data-driven algorithms, especially deep learning-based methods.
